title: Language comparison: shorter aligned passage controls
question: Does the eight-language length comparison remain stable on shorter aligned passages?
summary: Eight disjoint aligned blocks per language. English remains nearest to the manuscript in every block; all 64 known-language controls match their development profiles in each representation.

scope.representation: Existing rune-only joined LP2-00–55 token ledger, 2896 tokens, headings included; no decimal tokens. Three shared representations plus a Welsh digraph sensitivity; details in plan.
scope.procedure: For each block and representation, compare each language length histogram to the fixed manuscript histogram with the baseline TV metric. Report all scores and ranks, not a posterior. Classify each of 64 language/block profiles by nearest full dev language histogram, separately per representation; publish confusion matrices and individual decisions. Dev is unchanged; no fitting or tuning.
scope.parameters: Eight disjoint blocks from all 1,012 FLORES devtest sentences per language: four of 127 sentences, four of 126. Identical sentence ranges across languages; three fixed representations; no bootstrap.
scope.exclusions: No matched-length random samples, genre-matched corpus, known decoded LP control, cipher recovery or all-language inference. GP grouping remains an unvalidated orthographic sensitivity.

finding: English has the smallest manuscript length-distance in all eight blocks in each representation. Known-language reference matching succeeds in 64/64 decisions per representation. This is stability within FLORES, not proof of plaintext language.
limitations: Blocks match sentences, not token counts, and may share source articles; the 64 control decisions are not independent. Genre, cipher and transcription differences prevent a plaintext-language conclusion.
next_steps: Independently review tokenization; compare a fixed genre-matched parallel corpus and exact target-sized samples. Known LP reading controls are documented in a related record.

changes.before: Total variation distance between word-length histograms, bins 1..15 and16+. Lower is closer. Rank eight languages separately for each of first three representations. Never combine metrics into a language probability. IoC and within-word adjacent-identical fraction; separate distances under fixed bijective substitution only. Distinct symbol inventory reported. Dev language profiles classify each whole devtest language by word-length distance (8 held-out documents per representation). No tuning after scoring.
